title: REPORT on the 2023 and 2024 Commission reports on Ukraine
part_text: 48. Recalls that, since the start of the war in Ukraine, Poland has emerged as a major refuge for Ukrainians and provides extensive aid to Ukrainian refugees, including housing, financial assistance, access to education for children and medical care; deplores, therefore, the fact that Ukraine’s political establishment continues to see the Volhynia massacre as a war related only to the Ukrainians’ fight for their land; notes that Ukrainian Insurgent Army leaders Bandera and Shukhevych are seen as national heroes in Ukraine and that hundreds of streets, city squares and other landmarks are named after them; welcomes the fact that talks between the Polish and Ukrainian authorities have led to the resumption of the excavation of graves of Polish citizens on Ukrainian territory in April 2025; expects this process to be continued with the clear aim of providing the victims with a dignified burial and remembrance; insists that Ukraine fully address unresolved aspects of historical bilateral and regional relations in the spirit of true and sincere reconciliation;
